feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility and leadership in digital strategy, operations, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through specific platforms, tools, and scope details: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers.  
- Writing is generally strong, professional, and easy to follow, with a clear focus on mission-driven communications and cross-functional coordination.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, production savings, process efficiency, or campaign results. Several bullets describe responsibilities more than impact.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer senior-level value proposition would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior positioning and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, more executive summary of scope.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving cross-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and platform governance across web, email, social, and multimedia. Known for translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, accessible content and building the systems that enable effective advocacy and organizational communication.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is echoed throughout NACo roles; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Prioritize strategic, leadership-level competencies over tool-adjacent items already covered elsewhere.
- Consider a sharper version: Digital strategy & transformation • Content operations & editorial governance • Web platform & CMS leadership • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow & systems design • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production
- If space allows, replace “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform & CMS leadership” for stronger seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” “analytics,” and “multimedia” are already repeated in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “workflow & systems architecture” overlap with Technical + IT and could be framed more strategically.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time nature feel more senior and strategic.

Suggested edit
- Open with scale + remit: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-oriented lines, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance for coordinated cross-channel publishing.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, engagement lift, search success, or team/stakeholder count.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the header and NACo role—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor bullet and make outcome phrasing more decisive: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize leadership/scale, not routine oversight: “Oversaw enterprise email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for studio, analytics, and governance bullets—e.g., production volume, reporting adoption, time saved, publishing consistency, or decision-making speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video/studio language may overlap with the footer project list; focus here on building organizational capability, not content series details.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid mid-career progression item, but it reads as a bridge between the earlier producer role and the later director role. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable audience or production growth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show scope and leadership: “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-functional coordination.”
- Make newsletters more outcome-focused: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet with growth/ownership language: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add output, views, or engagement metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as scaling/owning the program rather than launching it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership/value angle and reflect the most recent enterprise, governance, and public-sector work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, outcome-oriented skill labels:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing “leadership,” “planning,” and “messaging” styles inconsistently.
- If space allows, make one line more distinctive with scale/context, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize current strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put most relevant/recent items first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations; de-emphasize older or less central platforms.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority platform from this topline section, e.g. SharePoint or Power Pages, unless it is central to target roles.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing coding languages alone to sound more outcome-oriented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep topline skills high-level and leave full platform/tool inventory below.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim multiple times.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making, not repeat software names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to impact-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business-facing language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive/leadership dashboards” instead of “leadership reporting”
- Consider revised line: “- Analytics strategy and reporting - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework development - Executive dashboards - SEO and digital performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; combine into one concise optimization phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line on “Multimedia production and livestream operations.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior phrasing: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • In-house studio operations”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the NACo studio build and leadership level.
- Drop “virtual” if keeping “hybrid event delivery”; hybrid already implies virtual/in-person integration.
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than tools alone: “Livestream and hybrid event production” reads stronger than just “Livestreaming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; use one for strategic scope and the other for execution detail.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” may feel too tactical unless the target role values hands-on production.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either be tightened or reframed to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS Platforms” for concision and consistency.
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest/least relevant item with a stronger platform-related capability already evidenced in experience, e.g. “CMS modernization” or “modular content architecture.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one version more strategic and this one purely tool-based.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector focus unless it supports a project you mention elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually relevant to recent work and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; it dates the section without adding value.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if still actively used in recent projects; otherwise remove it to keep the stack current.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used for CMS enhancements, tagging, automation, and lightweight edge scripting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” plus “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want cleaner category separation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to focus on systems you likely configured or used strategically: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move general collaboration tools out unless they were admin-level platforms: Slack, Teams, and Basecamp read as everyday workplace tools, not differentiating technical skills.
- Consider a sharper label: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” or “Automation, Integration & Work Management”
- If accurate, add scope in another section rather than here, e.g., “Built workflow automations in Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier to streamline editorial and cross-team processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same idea without added specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are partially redundant as generic project-management tools; keep only the strongest/current ones.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare to add much value on its own. It should better signal enterprise email/marketing automation capability and align with the stronger email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic Thrive Marketing • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief: enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, and journey automation
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest relevance: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Your work experience already establishes email leadership; avoid repeating generic “email newsletters” language here.
- If Dynamics 365 was only lightly used, don’t overstate it—Mailchimp may be less strategic unless tied to meaningful campaign or automation work.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, weekly video, and cross-channel operations. Make this entry more foundational: team-building, early platform/content wins, and scope of production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and foreground distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content; improved execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with stronger management language if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” repeats later operations language; frame this as early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy initiatives.”
- If possible, add a measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported member engagement.
- Keep it to 1–2 lines so it complements, rather than competes with, later digital leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/production language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize digital leadership here; save team-building and channel ownership for 2015–2024 roles.
